references.text: Cain is mentioned here as the ancestor of the Kenites. Balaam's prophecy refers to Cain's descendants and their future fate.
The Kenites are listed among the peoples in the land of Canaan that God promised to Abraham. This confirms the historical presence of the Kenites in the region.
The preceding verse introduces the prophecy about the Kenites and their dwelling place, which continues in verse 22.
The Kenites are mentioned as the people of Moses' father-in-law, who settled among the tribe of Judah. This shows the connection between the Kenites and Israel.
Heber the Kenite had separated from the other Kenites. The history of the Kenites continues after Balaam's prophecy.
The Kenites are mentioned in connection with the Amalekites. Saul warned them before the war, which shows their special position among the peoples.
Assyria (Asshur) is referred to as God's instrument for judgment. Balaam's prophecy points forward to Assyria's role in carrying people away into exile.
The land of the Kenites is mentioned as an area that David raided. This confirms the geographical presence of the Kenites in the Negev region.
